subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a static, jointless hovering pickup truck model made of simple primitives like boxes and lathes, roughly 5.2m long and 2.1m wide, planning to position it just above the ground plane in model space.

I'm deciding on the layout front-to-back—hood, cabin, bed—and figuring out how to build the body's lower side profile as an extrusion along the vehicle's width, listing out the (z,y) polygon points for that cross-section.

Next I'm sketching the cabin as a separate extrusion sitting above the lower body, defining its profile points to get the windshield slope and roofline, and planning window cutouts as decals.

Working out windscreen box placement...

Side windows at x=±0.86 need a slanted trapezoid shape with transparent cutaway outside, spanning z -0.3 to 1.2. For the body details, I'm planning a hood scoop, glowing vents, armor plates, a ram bar bumper, cyan/magenta headlight strips, a neon roof light bar, and a grille with a military star/hex stencil pattern, with paint leaning gunmetal and neon accents for the cyberpunk aesthetic.

For the hover thrusters, I'm placing four nacelles near the wheel positions, each with a mounting pylon, a vertical ducted-fan cylinder housing, a downward-facing glow disc, a glowing ring torus, and stabilizer fins, positioned just outside the body so the pods sit between y=0 and 0.45 near x=±1.2.

Writing lathe geometry profile...

Rather than a downward glow cone that'd clip through the floor, I'll add a glow ring on the outer rim edge near the base, plus a glowing fan disc with cross blades inside the shroud visible from the top, topped with a spiky intake cap.

For the rear hover unit, I'm adding a hub cylinder with six rotated blade boxes looping around it, a cyan glow disc beneath, and dark blades above so the glow peeks through from above. I'm also planning extras: rear exhaust stacks, a roof light bar with antenna and radar dish, a bed-mounted rocket launcher with six tube cylinders, spare crates, red glowing tail light strips, and magenta underglow strips along the sills.

Now I'm working on fender armor over the thruster pods with hazard-striped side skirts, plus decal planes for a "07" unit number and star emblem on the door and hood, positioning them precisely against the body's width and slope geometry, and adding a raised armor box on the hood to carry the top decal.

Next I'm defining the bed walls, tailgate, and cabin bulkhead dimensions, then planning out the texture set needed for visual variety—glass windows with teal-magenta reflections, door stencils, hood emblem, grille, hazard stripes, and license plate—to make sure I hit a good texture count for visual richness.

I'm sketching out the paint definitions for the body using camo mottling and countershading for depth, plus a basic helper function for creating box-shaped parts with consistent styling options.

For emissive parts I'll wrap them in a glow function using a palette of cyan, magenta, amber, and red, and I'm setting up rotation and cylinder-axis conventions so cylinders can be oriented along any axis using a direction vector. Now I'm working out the overall bounding dimensions -- bumper and ram bar extending toward the front, roof height constraints -- before actually writing the construction code.

Now I'm detailing the underside: adding a belly box with a hover-generator glow and magenta underglow strips, plus struts connecting the body to side pods at specific offsets, with pod positions placed symmetrically front-to-back along z.

For each pod I'm adding a fender flare over the wheel-arch and a small hub-and-blade fan structure, with a cylindrical hub and six radially-offset rotated blade boxes forming the rotor.

Still building the glow geometry and body extrusion...

Now I'm working out the cabin shape, extruding it with its own thickness and bevel, and adjusting the windshield slope coordinates since my earlier points didn't line up with the pillar geometry correctly.

Using dark flat glass color rather than textured. Now I'm working out the side window geometry - positioning the trapezoid on the cabin's side face, calculating where it intersects the roofline slope at different heights to get the correct window boundaries.

Writing windshield trapezoid shape...

Then I'll add door stencil decals on the lower body plane, positioned at the side door locations.

For the door text decal, I need to work out orientation so "HX-07" reads correctly from each side viewer's perspective — checking the right-vector math for both the left-side (s=-1) and right-side (s=1) planes confirms the local x-axis mapping to z works correctly for both.

Now for the hood decal, I'm figuring out the coordinate mapping with dir pointing up and up-hint toward z, which gives local x mapping to negative world x, so drawing right corresponds to the model's right when viewed from behind looking forward.

Working out the hood box dimensions and position — placing it roughly centered around y 1.2-1.3 and z 1.45-2.3, with the decal sitting at the top surface. Then I'm shaping the front grille area, with the body's front face sloping forward between z 2.7-2.8, and placing the grille plane just ahead of that slope around z 2.82, y 0.7.

Positioning the bumper bar and grille texture together — the bumper sits lower around y 0.42-0.58 so it hangs below the body bottom, while the grille plane sits above it around y 0.72-0.98 depending on how it aligns with the sloped front face. Adding headlight glow slits on either side of the grille, roughly at x ±0.7-0.8, y 0.75-0.76, small and thin.

Now I'm working out the rotation for a light bar across that sloped front face — calculating the slope direction between the two slope points to get the correct tilt angle, landing on roughly 33.7 degrees around the X axis so the bar sits flush against the slanted surface.

I'm placing a thin cyan DRL strip across the slope, offset slightly along the surface normal so it sits just above the body panel. Then I'm adding a roof lightbar positioned near the top, split into cyan and magenta glowing end segments for a police-style look, plus a thin antenna rod sticking up from the roof.

Now I'm adding a satellite dish on the roof made from a lathe-generated bowl shape, tilted back slightly. For the bed, I'm building a rotating turret assembly -- a cylindrical pedestal base, a boxy turret housing, twin barrels extending outward with glowing muzzle tips, a side armor shield, and a glowing ammo box, along with spare crates in the bed.

I'm now sketching out the bed walls and tailgate as thin boxes sized to fit the body's halfwidth, adding neon trim strips along the top edges in magenta, and placing glowing red tail light boxes near the rear face of the body.

Then I'm working out the rear bumper placement and a license plate decal plane, figuring out the correct local axis orientation so the plate text reads correctly for a viewer standing behind the vehicle looking forward.

Next I'm positioning the side skirts with armor boxes and hazard stripe decals along the lower doors, checking they clear the thruster strut zones, and adding thin magenta underglow strips just beneath the skirts near the body's bottom edge.

I'm now adding cabin extras: mirrors mounted on arms near the upper doors, vertical exhaust stacks behind the cabin with glowing cyan tops and clamp bands, and hood vent slits positioned to avoid overlapping the hood decal.

I'm widening the hood box and placing three vent slits on each side plus a centered decal, then adding armor plates at the front corners, angled bumper wings, an under-body hover generator block with glowing coil strips, a connecting cross bar, and rear canard stabilizer fins.

Now I'm defining tall extruded rear bed fins with an angular outline, painted dark armor color with a neon glow edge, and setting up a material palette of body paint, armor, dark trim, and neon accents, plus considering a small holographic sign plate on the bed bulkhead.

Writing texture SVGs...

Now I'm designing the hover thruster pods: a lathed armored shroud, hub, six blades, a glow disc, torus ring, strut, and mounting pad, plus small stabilizer fins and four glowing bolt spheres arranged in a ring near the top.

I'll bump the torus radius to .44 so it protrudes slightly past the wall for a glowing edge, then size the mirror strut box to sit centered around x=1.15 just below the pod top. With roughly 150 parts total, I should keep the module reasonably compact and make sure I import the right helpers for building, painting, and glow effects before writing the final code.

Writing helper functions...

Now I'm angling the roof dish's axis for a tilted lathe orientation, then adding turret barrels as cylinders with muzzle glow details at the tips, plus cargo crates and a fuel canister to round out the design before cleaning up the numbers in code.
